laura: FYI ran a 6hr perf sweep on streaming chat vs sync completions. saw a weird tail: p99 for streaming jumps when mb_size < 6.

mike: interesting — was that with prefix KV cache enabled?

laura: yes. KV cache hit rate steady ~98%, but tail spikes correlate with kernel fallback logs. example: `kernel_select: fallback_to_generic` at tail events.

samir: can you paste the short profile snippet?

laura: sure:
```
> PROFILE (sample):
>  - req id: bench-20260315-42
>  - model: redwood-3b-q4h
>  - mode: streaming
>  - mb_size: 4
>  - p50: 45ms/token, p95: 210ms/token, p99: 380ms/token
>  - kernel path: optimized_attn -> sometimes fallback to generic_attn (latency +120ms)
```

laura: fallback seems to happen when sequence length + active KV pages > threshold and we hit a kernel cache miss.

nina: got it. are batching heuristics different for streaming vs sync? iirc streaming uses short window + early flush, which can create more short batches.

mike: correct. streaming code uses `batcher.window_ms=6` and `batcher.flush_on_first_token=true`. sync uses window_ms=18 by default.

samir: hypothesis: small streaming batches increase kernel churn (more kernel_select calls) and expose cold kernel path. also KV eviction churn could evict compiled kernels or device scratch buffers.

laura: agreed. next experiment: bump streaming window to 12ms and cap mb_size to 8, force stable kernel selection by pre-warming.

mike: also try `kernel_selector.prefer_fast_path=true` so it biases to the optimized kernels even if memory is tight (we'll monitor OOMs).

nina: can we instrument kernel_select counts per minute and KV eviction events? that'll show correlation.

laura: already added a quick metric in bench harness: `kernel_fallback_count`, `kv_eviction_count`, `batch_count_by_size`. attaching quick run summary from today: 
```
run: streaming-window12-prewarm
mb_target: up to 8
kernel_fallback_count: 6/hr (was 54/hr)
kv_eviction_count: 3/hr (was 21/hr)
p50/p95/p99 tokens: 43/120/160 ms/token (vs 45/210/380 baseline)
throughput change: -6% overall token/s
```

ci-bench-bot: new benchmark recorded: bench-1965001234-streaming-window12-prewarm. link: https://bench.ci/1965001234

mike: nice tradeoff — small throughput loss but tail improved a lot. this looks promising for SLOs.

samir: for non-streaming completions (sync) do we see similar kernel fallback at small mb sizes?

laura: sync batchers coalesce more; p99 stays lower even when mb_size small because kernels have stable long-running allocations. only edge case is sudden seq-len spike.

nina: suggestion: implement a kernel warm-up pipeline for streaming where the first X requests per new model variant trigger a pre-compile pass for likely sequence-length buckets. cheap in aggregate.

mike: yeah — we can add a `warmup.profile_keys = [seq_len_buckets]` policy, run on model load. risk: added startup latency for model variant load, but acceptable for dedicated pools.

samir: also consider micro-slicing: let streaming produce logical microbatches but route them through a sticky executor for N seconds so kernel and buffers stay hot. minimal router change.

laura: implemented a prototype sticky-executor flag in bench: `executor.sticky_window_ms=2000`. numbers:
```
sticky run:
kernel_fallback_count: 2/hr
kv_eviction_count: 1/hr
p99: 140ms/token
throughput delta: -3%
```

laura: main takeaway: for streaming chat we need slightly larger temporal batching (12ms vs 6ms) + kernel warmup/sticky executors to hit p99 SLOs. sync completions can stay aggressive for throughput.

mike: action items:
- laura: open RFC with config defaults + bench artifacts.
- samir: add kernel_select and kv_eviction metrics to infra dashboards.
- nina: prototype warmup job for model variants (dedicated first).

nina: I'll start a spike and tag infra for dashboard panels.

laura: RFC created: https://go.redwood/rfcs/streaming-kernel-warmup-1965001234. attached microbench graphs.

samir: one more ask — add a p99 SLA smoke test that runs every deploy to ensure we don't regress fallback counts.

mike: agree. create CI alert if kernel_fallback_count increases >50% over baseline.

laura: noted, will add alerts and run a wider fleet sweep next week. :thumbsup:

ci-bench-bot: reminder — scheduled sweep: 1965002000 (fleet-wide).

mike: thanks everyone. we'll reconvene after the fleet sweep results.
